what_it_does: Many AI and scientific computations involve multiplying matrices (tables of numbers) where most entries are zero — called sparse matrices. Sparse matrix multiplication (SpMM) can be dramatically faster than working with all the zeros, but only if the software is tuned to the specific 'shape' of the sparsity (how the non-zero values are distributed). Writing hand-tuned code for every possible sparsity pattern is impractical, and generic compilers (programs that translate code into machine instructions) produce slow output. SpMMTC is a compiler that inspects the actual non-zero distribution of an input matrix at compile time, then automatically generates fast, vectorized code (code that processes multiple numbers simultaneously using the processor's SIMD units — wide registers that do many additions or multiplications at once) specifically matched to that pattern and to the hardware's memory hierarchy. This removes the need for manual tuning while still producing efficient code for a wide variety of sparse patterns and hardware targets.
